A_target.statement:
The number of [[Definition:Surjection|surjections]] from an $n$-set onto a $k$-set is:
:$\displaystyle \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^k \paren {-1}^j \binom k j \paren {k - j}^n = k! \, \map S {n, k}$
where $\map S {n, k}$ is a [[Definition:Stirling Numbers of the Second Kind|Stirling number of the second kind]].

B_source.statement:
Let $A_1, \ldots, A_k$ be finite sets.
Then:
:$\displaystyle \card {\bigcup_{i \mathop = 1}^k A_i} = \sum_{\O \mathop \ne S} \paren {-1}^{\card S + 1} \card {\bigcap_{i \mathop \in S} A_i}$

substitutions.the sets A_i: the functions missing the value i

object_map.reformulation: Count non-surjective functions by the values they miss.

validity_conditions: Functions missing every value in S are the functions into the remaining k - |S| values.
Grouping surjections by their fibres gives the Stirling number interpretation.
proof_plan:
Let $A_i$ be the set of functions $\set {1, \ldots, n} \to \set {1, \ldots, k}$ not taking the value $i$.
The surjections number $k^n - \card {\bigcup_i A_i}$.
For $\card S = j$, $\card {\bigcap_{i \in S} A_i} = \paren {k - j}^n$.
By the source result, the number of surjections is $\displaystyle \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^k \paren {-1}^j \binom k j \paren {k - j}^n$.
